process_issues.description: Built 'Option C' (bridge the app's Google login token into opencode for Gemini) as a full TDD subagent feature, then fully reverted it (commit 852f3fa -> revert 336099f) after discovering opencode's gemini-cli auth uses Google's OWN OAuth client (681...apps.googleusercontent.com), not the app's. A 2-minute probe of `opencode mcp ... getOAuthUrl('google')` / the gemini-auth plugin up front would have shown the wrong premise. I had even said 'verify feasibility before building' and built anyway. Lesson: for a workaround against an opaque dependency, probe the actual runtime auth/registration mechanism BEFORE building.
process_issues.detected_by: user manual smoke (sign-in dialog hang) + post-hoc binary/plugin inspection

process_issues.description: Claimed the MCP Connect/OAuth fix 'works' while the running api_server was a non-watch tsx process holding pre-fix in-memory code; the user's smoke failed twice ('connect button still doesnt open browser') before I realized relaunches were required. Lesson: after backend edits, the embedded tsx engine is NOT watch-mode -> a restart is mandatory before claiming a fix; verify the running PID's start-time/code, not just the on-disk source.
process_issues.detected_by: user manual smoke + lsof/ps on the running PID

process_issues.description: Repeated `flutter run` relaunches omitted the GOOGLE_DESKTOP_CLIENT_ID dart-define (release/CI bakes it in), so when the user's persisted session expired they were locked out of login on my dev build. Lesson: when hot-testing a release-configured app via `flutter run`, pass the same --dart-define set the release uses (recover public client ids from the installed .app), or script it.

HIGHEST-VALUE FINDING. The api_server test suite runs against SQLite only; production runs Postgres via postgres_bootstrap.ts. Two columns (integration_accounts.status/error_message; users.timezone) were added to the SQLite migrations + Postgres CREATE block but NEVER given Postgres `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` backfills (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS does not alter pre-existing prod tables). 901 green SQLite tests caught none of it; production Google sign-in 500'd on a fresh login, twice. Fixed in PR #732 (backfills) + manual prod ALTERs. Lesson: verification must exercise the PRODUCTION data engine, not just the dev one; a CI step that boots Postgres + runs bootstrap + a smoke write would have caught both before users.
process_issues.detected_by: production 500 + docker logs (real Postgres exception) after merge/relaunch

process_issues.description: PR #729 accumulated multiple unrelated efforts (curated MCP autoinstall, self-built remote MCP OAuth, inspector parity, streaming terminal, resizable panel, agent-identity fix, native Google Gemini). Offered to split; user opted to keep monolithic and merge. Reviewable history suffers. Lesson: spin a fresh branch/PR per independent concern even within one interactive session.

expected_chain: workflow-orchestrator (default entry for plan/implement/PR work in an AGENTS.md repo)
planning-agent / issue-writer for the feature decomposition
per work item: acceptance-contract -> coding-agent -> verification-gate -> (failure-triage -> repair -> re-gate)
observed_chain: Interactive main-loop drove everything; workflow-orchestrator / AgentFlow never invoked

Implementation slices dispatched as ad-hoc general-purpose TDD subagents (mcp_oauth_service, credentials dialog, badge resolver, gemini routing, projectId auto-config) — each red->green + tsc + atomic commit
Verification was in-line (subagent test runs + live smoke/curl + user UI smoke) rather than the verification-gate skill
project-state.md / decisions.md / memory updated manually by the main loop
Production incident (login 500) debugged reactively; root-caused by inspection (no prod log access initially, then docker logs)
PRs #732 then #729 merged and desktop v18.47 released on EXPLICIT user instruction

issues.description: A large multi-PR feature + incident effort ran with zero orchestrator routing. Much of it (live production-login debugging, iterative UI smoke, opaque-dependency OAuth spelunking) is genuinely exploratory and a poor fit for the plan->implement->verify chain; but the discrete implementation slices (OAuth service, credentials dialog, badge, gemini routing, projectId) could have gone acceptance-contract -> coding-agent -> verification-gate. The lighter ad-hoc TDD-subagent path preserved test discipline but skipped the formal gates and the postmortem loop.

Neither the gate nor smoke design surfaced the SQLite-vs-Postgres schema-drift class — verification ran only the dev DB engine. Two prod-only 500s reached the user. A generalizable rule ('verify against the production data engine / boot the prod DB in CI') would have caught it.

notes: Not a workflow-orchestrator run; scored 'bypassed' honestly. Strengths: evidence-based debugging (opencode logs, binary strings, isolated repro), honest course-correction (reverted the wrong-premise Option C; retracted the 'opencode can't use google' over-conclusion when the user pushed back), per-slice TDD + atomic commits, durable knowledge captured (memory: gemini-workspace setup + opencode MCP OAuth; decisions.md: per-user agent ACL deferral). scripts/mine-patterns.py is absent in this repo so the machine loop cannot consume this postmortem here. The single most reusable lesson is the prod-DB-engine verification gap (postgres_bootstrap drift).
